question: Should OpenClaw own `wiki apply-batch` and `wiki search-batch` as documented, versioned bundled Memory Wiki CLI contracts for automation?
rationale: The implementation adds a new public CLI surface rather than repairing a defined broken contract; code review and proof can establish safety, but they cannot choose the long-term ownership and compatibility commitment.

options.title: Sponsor the bounded CLI contract
options.body: Accept the two constrained batch commands as supported Memory Wiki automation APIs while preserving the existing single-operation commands.

options.title: Keep automation outside the bundled CLI
options.body: Decline the new public contract and direct callers to existing individual commands or a future externally owned integration if the long-term surface is not desired.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the bounded CLI contract
recommendation.body: Accept the two constrained batch commands as supported Memory Wiki automation APIs while preserving the existing single-operation commands.

likelyOwner.reason: Current project Vision and memory/plugin scope history make this the most evidence-backed owner candidate for the bundled-plugin contract decision.
